title: Household-level flood risk is concentrated among high-income property owners, with uninsured low-income vulnerability
discussion_signal: The NBER post translates the paper's household-level result: floodplain migration and aggregate exposure trends can look different from the distribution of risk across households. It highlights disproportionate exposure among high-income property owners while retaining the important counterpoint that low-income uninsured homeowners remain vulnerable. This makes exposure, ownership, and insurance status separate social mechanisms rather than one aggregate risk measure.
linked_research_question: When aggregate flood exposure rises but household exposure shares remain stable, which combinations of ownership, building type, migration, and insurance determine who can actually recover from a flood?
limits: The post is a short institutional summary and does not provide the confidential-data sample count or all estimates
Exposure and insurance status do not establish adequate coverage, safe occupancy, repair, or recovery
A single institutional LinkedIn post is not representative of affected households or local communities
